item.title: Sphera Media Lab 2026: Open Call for Masterclasses and Keynotes
item.description:
Organisation: European Lab (Arty Farty) and the Sphera Network, coordinated by Medianes

Location: LaVallee, Rue Adolphe Lavallee 39, 1080 Brussels, Belgium. Proposals are accepted regardless of where you are based, but they should reflect a European perspective.

Award: Selected contributors receive a fee plus travel to Brussels and accommodation, all covered by the organisers. The fee amount is not published in the call. No submission fee.

Duration: One-day event on 3 December 2026; contributors deliver a single masterclass or keynote

Deadline: 31 Aug 2026

European Lab and the Sphera Network are opening submissions for the discourse programme of the next Sphera Media Lab, the annual forum for people defending independent media in Europe. THEMES: technological independence (sovereignty, tools, mutualisation); economic independence (cooperative models); editorial independence (press freedom, resisting the far right). FORMATS SOUGHT: masterclasses, led by an expert sharing advanced knowledge, technique and hands-on insight; and keynotes, inspiring talks grounded in a specific case study. WHO CAN PROPOSE: media outlets, associations, researchers and professionals. The organisers state they pay particular attention to parity and diversity across their programmes and ask that proposals take those criteria into account. WHAT IS COVERED: selected contributors travel to Brussels with transport, accommodation and a fee covered. THE EVENT: Sphera Media Lab 2026 runs on 3 December 2026 at LaVallee in Brussels, a full day of conferences, masterclasses and workshops for independent media professionals from across Europe, alongside the premiere of a documentary on threats facing European journalists. APPLICATION: submit your masterclass or keynote proposal via the Typeform at arty-farty.typeform.com/to/xnDikGGM before 31 August 2026.

item.title: Inato Gallery: Touch Some Grass (open-call poster exhibition)
item.description:
Organisation: Inato Gallery

Location: Submissions are digital (A3 portrait PDF) and no residency or travel is required; the exhibition is mounted by Inato Gallery, an artist-run space in Iligan City, Philippines. No nationality restriction is stated.

Award: No artist fee, stipend or production budget. This is an exhibition opportunity: selected posters are shown in Inato Gallery's Touch Some Grass exhibition. No submission fee is stated in the call.

Duration: One-off poster exhibition. Exhibition dates are not announced yet.

Deadline: 31 Aug 2026

Touch Some Grass is an open-call poster exhibition responding to the growing presence of AI-generated imagery and its impact on creative labour, authorship and visual culture. At a time when images can be produced instantly and consumed just as quickly, the exhibition reclaims the poster as a space for ideas, intention and public conversation, inviting artists to make work that questions, challenges or reflects on this changing landscape. As the organisers put it, the question is no longer whether machines can make images, they can; the question is what kind of world we build when speed matters more than thought. NOTE: this call offers exhibition and visibility only, with no artist fee or stipend. SUBMISSION GUIDELINES: artwork size A3 (297 x 420 mm), portrait orientation, 300 DPI, CMYK recommended, print-quality PDF preferred, maximum file size 1 GB, one submission per artist. CAP: participation is limited to 60 artists and the submission form closes automatically once all slots are filled, so the effective deadline may fall well before 31 August 2026 (10 of 60 slots were taken at the time of listing). Inato Gallery is an artist-run space in Iligan City, Philippines, which began as a solo street exhibition by KaraTula and now runs concept-driven solo and group shows, open mics, talks and workshops built on openness, participation and the belief that art should exist where people already are.

item.title: Ars Biologica ArtXScience Residency 2027-2028 (Ars Electronica x Ceske Budejovice ECoC 2028)
item.description:
Organisation: Ars Electronica and Ceske Budejovice - European Capital of Culture 2028

Location: Ceske Budejovice, Czech Republic. Open to applicants of any nationality aged 18+ who are legally eligible to work and travel in the EU. Required on-site stays: up to one month in February/March 2027, an optional stay in August/September 2027, and March 2028 for installation, exhibition and deinstallation.

Award: EUR 24,000 total package per winner: EUR 6,000 artist fee, up to EUR 15,000 production budget, and up to EUR 3,000 for travel, accommodation and subsistence, plus a separate budget covering one month of housing in Ceske Budejovice. Two positions available. Free to apply.

Duration: January 2027 to April 2028, with on-site blocks in early 2027 and March 2028

Deadline: 28 Sep 2026

A fully funded art-science residency from Ars Electronica and Ceske Budejovice, European Capital of Culture 2028, exploring how art and science can collaborate on urgent environmental challenges: climate emergence, sustainable agriculture, geoengineering, permaculture, water resource management, and the broader ecological impacts on local communities. Selected residents work in direct collaboration with local scientists in Ceske Budejovice. WHO CAN APPLY: artists, designers, creatives and artist collectives with more than 5 years of professional creative practice and documented interdisciplinary work; experience in community engagement and science collaborations is essential; applicants must be 18+, of any nationality, and legally eligible to work and travel in the EU. WHAT YOU GET: a EUR 24,000 package (EUR 6,000 artist fee, up to EUR 15,000 production, up to EUR 3,000 travel and subsistence) plus one month of housing covered separately; two winners are selected. STRUCTURE: the residency runs January 2027 to April 2028, with a required on-site stay of up to one month in February/March 2027, an optional stay in August/September 2027, and a March 2028 stay for festival installation, exhibition and deinstallation. HOW TO APPLY: online form with project title, a written proposal of max 250 words, a scientific direction statement (max 100 words), artistic vision (max 100 words), community connection plan (max 100 words), a super short pitch (3 to 30 words), 3 to 7 images, an optional 1-minute video, a portfolio link and contact information. Two-round selection (online application then interview); winners notified by November 2026. Deadline 28 September 2026 at midnight CET.

item.title: Perform Europe: Third Open Call for Cross-Border Touring (2026-28 edition)
item.description:
Organisation: Perform Europe (IETM, EFA, Circostrada, European Dancehouse Network, Pearle*, IDEA Consult), co-funded by Creative Europe

Location: Europe-wide; touring must happen in at least 3 Creative Europe countries. The UK is NOT eligible.

Award: Three grant tiers of EUR 15,000, EUR 25,000 or EUR 55,000, plus top-ups of up to EUR 5,000, giving a EUR 60,000 ceiling per partnership. EUR 1.4 million total across at least 25 partnerships, covering up to 100 percent of eligible costs, so no matching funds are needed. TOP-UP RATES: green mobility EUR 400 per person per presentation date; accessibility support EUR 400 per person per presentation date; family top-up EUR 200 per child per presentation date; audience access EUR 800 per presentation date; visa EUR 120 per person needing one; overseas and outermost regions EUR 175 per person per presentation date. No application fee.

Duration: Touring and implementation 1 March 2027 to 31 January 2028 (11 months).

Deadline: 22 Oct 2026

Perform Europe is the EU's dedicated cross-border touring scheme for the performing arts, run by a six-organisation consortium and co-funded by Creative Europe. It funds partnerships of at least three organisations from three different Creative Europe countries to tour a finished performing arts work in at least three countries, with an explicit emphasis on greener, more inclusive and more equitable touring practice. Eligible disciplines are circus, dance, outdoor arts, performance art, puppetry and theatre; LIVE MUSIC AND OPERA ARE EXCLUDED, and production costs for new creations are not covered since the work must already be finished before 1 March 2027. Applicants pick one of three grant tiers with no fixed criteria per tier, and may request up to EUR 5,000 in top-ups for accessibility and sustainability measures. Five percent of the total fund is ring-fenced for proposals involving Ukrainian partners or supporting the Ukrainian performing arts sector. All 41 Creative Europe countries are eligible, including Albania, Armenia, Bosnia and Herzegovina, Georgia, Iceland, Kosovo, Liechtenstein, Moldova, Montenegro, North Macedonia, Norway, Serbia, Tunisia and Ukraine, but the UK is not. TIMING: applications close 22 October 2026 at 23:59 CEST, selected partnerships are announced in January 2027, and activity may only start from 1 March 2027. A Matchmaking Platform with over 2,300 registered professionals is available for finding partners before applying. CORE PRIORITY: each partnership must pick either diversity and inclusion or the fight against climate change as its core priority, and must also include measures addressing the other one; that choice has to run visibly through the whole application rather than sit in one section. WHO COUNTS AS A PARTNER: both organisations and individual professionals are eligible, so a partner can be an artist, collective, company, producer, presenter, venue, festival, residency, educational institution or NGO. Eligibility is decided by where you are legally based. The partnership appoints a lead partner who submits, signs and receives the grant. ELIGIBLE COSTS: artistic fees and salaries, travel, accommodation, subsistence, administration, reporting, communication, translation, surtitling, equipment transport, copyright fees, access and environmental measures, complementary activities and capacity building. Venue and equipment rental or purchase is capped at 5 percent of the requested grant, and preparation costs for presenting an existing work at 10 percent. PAYMENT: 60 percent after signing, 20 percent after the first narrative and financial report is approved, and the final 20 percent after completion and EU approval of Perform Europe's own final report. Top-ups are reimbursed only after the project ends and documentation is approved, so budget for the cash-flow gap. PRACTICAL: every partner must register for a Perform Europe account before submission and approval can take several working days, so do not leave that to the last week.

item.title: Video Pool: Media Art + Technology Residency (MATR) 2027
item.description:
Organisation: Video Pool Media Arts Centre

Location: In person at Video Pool Media Arts Centre and its Poolside Gallery, 221-100 Arthur Street, Winnipeg, Manitoba R3B 1H3, Canada.

Award: CAD 2,250 artist fee, covering both the residency period and the subsequent Poolside Gallery exhibition. Residents also get full access to VP's equipment, facilities and technical resources; the Poolside Gallery itself is equipped with two projectors and four speakers. Applicants must be VP members, so a membership is purchased separately, but there is no separate application fee.

Duration: Up to two months to develop and install the project, including one month of dedicated access to the Poolside Gallery. Residency takes place in Winter 2027; exhibition dates TBD.

Deadline: 30 Aug 2026

Video Pool's Media Art + Technology Residency supports experimental, independent, technology-based work. The selected artist or artists develop a new project (or adapt and transform an existing one) in direct response to the intimate scale and specific character of the Poolside Gallery, culminating in an exhibition there. The call is deliberately open on medium: video, sound, installation, digital media, performance, interactive technologies, expanded cinema and interdisciplinary practices are all welcome. VP asks proposals to speak clearly to your practice, the questions, materials or ideas that drive the work, and how that work might grow, shift or take new form inside the gallery. It is explicitly interested in expansive proposals, work that pushes past the gallery's four walls to engage its surrounding spaces (hallways, windows, projection wall) or that reimagines what the gallery itself can hold, and in projects that engage technology as a creative, critical, aesthetic or socio-political tool. Priority is given to artists from equity-seeking communities whose practices contribute to the advancement of experimental media arts. Residents get full access to VP's available equipment, facilities and technical resources throughout the residency, and applicants are encouraged to review the equipment and facilities list before proposing. ELIGIBILITY: open to VP members (this is a member submission call); no nationality restriction is stated, but the residency and exhibition are in person in Winnipeg. APPLICATION: artist bio (1,500 characters), headshot, description of your artistic practice (3,000 characters), project proposal for MATR (3,000 characters), equipment and facility needs (750 characters), description of how you would use the space (750 characters), CV, up to five images (optional) and up to two video or documentation links. Submit via the online form at videopool.org/matr-2027-application/ by 30 August 2026; alternative submission formats can be arranged by contacting Emma (emma@videopool.org) or Iyunade (iyunade@videopool.org). General enquiries: info@videopool.org, 204-949-9134.

item.title: Stimuleringsfonds: Open Call Residency Videotage 2027 (Hong Kong)
item.description:
Organisation: Stimuleringsfonds Creatieve Industrie (Creative Industries Fund NL) in collaboration with Videotage, Hong Kong

Location: Residency takes place at Videotage in Hong Kong. Applicants must be established in the Netherlands, Aruba, Bonaire, Curacao, Saba, Sint Eustatius or Sint Maarten (Kingdom of the Netherlands) and registered in a business register within the Kingdom of the Netherlands.

Award: EUR 5,000 for a two-month residency or EUR 6,500 for a three-month residency, paid by the Creative Industries Fund NL to cover travel, insurance, living expenses, compensation for time invested, and material and transport costs. Accommodation, use of the studio space and facilitation by Videotage are covered directly by the Fund on top of this. No application fee.

Duration: Two or three months in 2027 (spring 2027); state your preferred period in the application.

Deadline: 21 Oct 2026

The Creative Industries Fund NL (Stimuleringsfonds) runs this residency with Videotage, a Hong Kong-based non-profit media arts institution specialising in the promotion, presentation, creation and preservation of moving image and media art in all forms and languages. The Fund is recruiting one Netherlands-based designer, maker or observer working in digital culture to spend two or three months at Videotage's studio space in Hong Kong in 2027, conducting research, broadening their network, developing new work inspired by Hong Kong, and presenting their findings or completed works. The residency encourages crossovers and experimentation, giving the participant space to explore new methodologies, widen their creative practice and produce work that pushes the boundaries of digital culture, with a focus on social and urban dynamics. The 2027 edition takes the technological 'black box' phenomenon as its starting point and invites the resident to respond to that theme within the context of Videotage. ELIGIBILITY: you are an individual designer, maker or observer within the field of digital culture; you are established in the Netherlands, Aruba, Bonaire, Curacao, Saba, Sint Eustatius or Sint Maarten (Kingdom of the Netherlands); you are registered in the business register of the Dutch Chamber of Commerce (KvK) or another business register within the Kingdom of the Netherlands; and you have had a professional practice in the creative industry for at least four years. NOT open to duos, collectives or cooperative ventures, nor to designers and makers who receive a grant during the work period under the Talent Development Grant Scheme, the Open Call Self-taught Designer or the Open Call Emerging Design Practices ABCSSS. Note that accepting this open call means you cannot apply to those schemes and open calls in 2027. FUNDING: EUR 5,000 for two months or EUR 6,500 for three months, covering travel, insurance, living expenses, compensation for time invested and material and transport costs; accommodation, studio use and Videotage's facilitation are covered separately by the Fund. Submit your proposal to the Creative Industries Fund NL by 21 October 2026, 16:00 CEST.

item.title: Statens Kunstfond: Production and Exhibitions, Contemporary Art in Denmark and Abroad (2026 autumn round)
item.description:
Organisation: Statens Kunstfond (Danish Arts Foundation)

Location: Denmark and abroad. Non-Danish venues and organisations may apply, but only for exhibitions that feature Danish artists.

Award: DKK. No published minimum or maximum; the committee assesses each application on its merits and historical awards are published on the site. No stated co-financing requirement. No application fee. Applications must be submitted digitally via the Danish subsidy portal (Tilskudsportalen).

Duration: Project-length; production and exhibition periods vary.

Deadline: 24 Sep 2026

The Danish Arts Foundation's Production and Exhibitions programme funds the production, dissemination and exhibition of contemporary art in Denmark and abroad, and it is one of the few Nordic national schemes a foreign organisation can apply to directly. Eligible costs include creating new works where an exhibition agreement is in place, exhibition costs, exhibition programming featuring Danish or international artists, promotion tied to an exhibition, and honorariums covering artists' work and installation time, which lets a festival or biennial cover commission and artist-fee lines. THE KEY CONDITION for non-Danish applicants is that the exhibition must feature Danish artists; Danish artists and venues face no such restriction. No minimum or maximum grant is published since the committee decides case by case, and previous award levels are visible on the site. Two 2026 deadlines apply: 26 March 2026 (closed) and 24 September 2026 at 14:00, with the application form opening one month before each deadline. TIMING: applicants receive a response no later than twelve weeks after the deadline, so expect a decision by mid-December 2026. Applications must go through the Danish digital subsidy portal; submissions outside it are rejected except in very special circumstances. FLAG: earliest-start-date rules are not specified on the funder's page.

item.title: JUGAAD: Absolute Improvisation, open call for printed matter and small-format works (Amsterdam)
item.description:
Organisation: SAC Art Amsterdam and Mama Magnet

Location: Fair takes place 9-10 October 2026 in Amsterdam. Open internationally, but selected work must be shipped to the Netherlands by the end of September 2026 at the artist's expense.

Award: No application fee. Selected work is sold at the printed matter fair on mutually agreeable terms regarding commission, duration and number of editions; artists are remunerated within 30 days of each sale. Unsold works are returned at the end of the agreed consignment period.

Duration: Rolling selection 5 August to 5 September 2026; fair 9-10 October 2026

Deadline: 05 Sep 2026

Open call from SAC Art Amsterdam and Mama Magnet for a printed matter fair themed around jugaad: improvised, resourceful solutions built from what is on hand (from the Sanskrit yuj, 'to join', via Hindi jugar, famously embodied by post-independence Punjabi vehicles pieced together from scrap metal and pump engines). The curators want work that engages the spirit of jugaad either as subject (everyday intelligences of getting by, lateral logics of adaptation, unlikely workarounds, reinvention born of necessity) or in how it was made (found or repurposed materials, adapted processes, structures built to solve a specific constraint). Work that came from adjustment rather than access, problem-solving rather than budget. WHAT: zines, artist books, comics, risograph or photocopied prints, posters, foldables, instruction manuals, packaging and other small-format works; if it can travel in a suitcase it is probably in scope. No framed work or anything needing gallery-standard installation. Gen-AI images and text are not accepted. WHO: artists, designers, writers and collectives whose practice genuinely engages with the theme; if unsure, reach out and explain in a line or two. Selected work must reach the Netherlands by end of September 2026. TERMS: selections made on a rolling basis 5 August to 5 September; selected work is sold at the fair (9-10 October, Amsterdam) on mutually agreeable commission terms, with payment within 30 days of each sale and unsold work returned after the consignment period. HOW TO APPLY: email info@mamamagnet.org with a CC to art@sacartamsterdam.com, subject line 'JUGAAD - [Your Contribution]', by 5 September 2026; earlier is better given rolling selection.

item.title: CPR Center for Performance Research: Artist-in-Residence Program 2027
item.description:
Organisation: CPR - Center for Performance Research

Location: Brooklyn, New York City, USA. RESTRICTED: NYC-based artists only; CPR does not sponsor visas, and residents must remain NYC-based for the whole cycle.

Award: $2,000 stipend, 20 free hours of rehearsal space, up to 150 subsidised rehearsal hours across CPR's two studios with priority and advance booking, presentation slots in the OPEN LAB and OPEN AiR programmes, and access to technical equipment and production support. No application fee.

Duration: One year, January to December 2027

Deadline: Closed 24 Aug 2026

CPR's year-long Artist-in-Residence programme supports six New York City-based artists working across contemporary dance, performance and time-based art. The organisation values experimental approaches to content, form and aesthetics and explicitly encourages risk-taking, interdisciplinarity and the unexpected, so process-led and hard-to-categorise work is in scope rather than a liability. WHAT RESIDENTS RECEIVE: a $2,000 stipend; 20 free hours of rehearsal space plus up to 150 further subsidised hours in CPR's two studios, with priority and advance calendar access; participation in OPEN LAB (facilitated embodied workshops and feedback showings) and OPEN AiR (solo or shared presentations of current work); and access to technical equipment and production support. ELIGIBILITY: artists must be based in New York City and remain so throughout the cycle (no visa sponsorship); must have had work publicly presented before; must not have held a CPR residency in the last five years; and current undergraduates are not eligible. Individuals, companies, collaboratives and collectives may all apply, each counting as a single residency. CPR strongly encourages applications from BIPOC, LGBTQ+, immigrant and disabled artists and from artists across generations. APPLICATION: a Google Form with narrative answers on the artist's central research focus and its alignment with CPR's values; drafting answers in a separate document first is recommended. Selection is by an independent panel of artists, curators and arts leaders. Deadline: Monday 24 August 2026 at 5pm ET; late submissions are not accepted. Notifications November 2026. Questions: applications@cprnyc.org.

item.title: Kulturdirektoratet: Cross-Disciplinary Cultural Activity, Events, Organisers and Venues (2026 autumn round)
item.description:
Organisation: Kulturdirektoratet (Arts and Culture Norway)

Location: Norway. Activity is expected to take place in Norway, though international artists and partners can be programmed.

Award: NOK. No fixed minimum or maximum published; grant sizes are assessed against the project budget, financing plan and available funds. Kulturdirektoratet states it does not provide full financing, so co-financing is required in practice but no fixed percentage is set. Historical award levels are published in the scheme's public decision database. No application fee.

Duration: Project grants for single events or series; activity grants cover the 2027 operating year.

Deadline: 15 Sep 2026

Kulturdirektoratet's main scheme for multi-artistic and cross-disciplinary events, organisers and venues, and the natural Norwegian route for a festival or biennial that does not sit inside a single artform committee. It funds single events, event series, festivals and seminars with cross-disciplinary relevance, plus year-round operation of organisations with a multi-artistic profile, which covers media arts, digital culture and experimental sound programming presented alongside other forms. Art production itself, closed workshops, infrastructure investment and activity already completed before the deadline are not funded. Two application rounds run in 2026: 8 April 2026 (project grants, closed) and 15 September 2026 at 13:00 (project grants plus activity grants for the 2027 operating year). Project grants accept individuals, private and public institutions, and organisations, while activity grants require an organisation number or a named, separately budgeted activity within a larger entity, existing for at least one year and not already receiving permanent annual state funding. The scheme never fully finances a project, so a credible co-financing plan is expected. FLAG: decision dates and foreign-applicant eligibility are not published on the scheme page; award notifications arrive via the application portal.

item.title: Studio ALTA Residence 2027: four residency open calls (Prague)
item.description:
Organisation: Studio ALTA

Location: Studio ALTA, Prague (Liben district), Czech Republic. Three of the four calls are open internationally; the Rest House call is reserved for supporting-profession arts workers active in the Czech independent sector.

Award: Residency fees paid to participants: Research House CZK 12,000 per project; Rest House CZK 6,000 per person; House in the Neighborhood CZK 30,000 per project; House of Sweat CZK 15,000 per project. All include workspace at Studio ALTA; the two production residencies add dramaturgic, production, technical and PR support. Free to apply.

Duration: Programme dependent: 5 to 10 days, at various points between February and November 2027

Deadline: 10 Sep 2026

Prague performance venue Studio ALTA announces four residency open calls for 2027, all with a single deadline of 10 September 2026. RESEARCH HOUSE (19 to 28 April 2027): a shared residential laboratory for three art projects or individual artists in the early stages of exploration and experimentation, or reopening an existing finished work (performance, installation, object, video) to transform it into another form such as a workshop, text or performance-lecture. Includes a 10-day residency, a fee of CZK 12,000 per project, shared studio, individual workspace and facilitated exchange meetings; the research output must be shared publicly as a work-in-progress in a form based on participants' needs. REST HOUSE (March to November 2027): a five-day residential spa for overloaded colleagues from the arts sector, with no required output or activities; restricted to people working in production, dramaturgy, curation, PR, technical and other supporting artistic professions in the Czech independent sector. Two guests are chosen by lottery (fee CZK 6,000 per person); the public draw is announced 16 September 2026. HOUSE IN THE NEIGHBORHOOD (9 to 18 August 2027): for one performative art project created with the local community and designed or adapted for public space in Liben and its surroundings; this year's call focuses on the 55+ target group. Includes a fee of CZK 30,000 per project, rehearsal and indoor facilities (primarily outdoor spaces), dramaturgic, production, technical and PR consultation, connections to partner organisations, and 7 days of intensive production and technical support in the final phase. A public premiere or work-in-progress in public space at the end of the residency is required. HOUSE OF SWEAT (1 to 10 February 2027): for one performative art project designed or adapted for the specific environment of the Studio ALTA sauna and its immediate surroundings, seeking new ways of working with intimate space, proximity to the audience and non-traditional formats. Includes a fee of CZK 15,000 per project, a 10-day residency, sauna and rehearsal spaces, dramaturgic, production, technical and PR consultation, and 2 days of intensive final-phase support; a public work-in-progress or premiere in the sauna within the 9 to 12 February 2027 programme block is required. Projects at any stage of development can apply to the production calls, and selected projects may be included in Studio ALTA's year-round programme. TIMELINE: deadline 10 September 2026; results 3 weeks after the deadline (30 September 2026); a Q&A Zoom call takes place 10 August 2026 at 3:00 PM. Apply via the registration forms on the call page.

item.title: Accion Cultural Espanola: PICE Movilidad 2026 (Phase 3)
item.description:
Organisation: Accion Cultural Espanola (AC/E)

Location: Anywhere outside Spain, at the applicant's own venue or event. Applicant must be a foreign entity constituted outside Spain.

Award: Max EUR 15,000 per applicant per call, per event and per thematic area; within that, max EUR 5,000 per participant or collective. Total 2026 call budget EUR 1,810,000 (Musica y creacion sonora EUR 320,000, Artes visuales EUR 200,000, Videojuego y animacion EUR 90,000, Arquitectura y diseno EUR 90,000, Podcast EUR 90,000). Mandatory co-financing: the applicant must commit at least 50 percent of each proposal's total budget. No application fee.

Duration: Single event or project; Phase 3 activities must start on or after 1 November 2026 and finish before 28 February 2027.

Deadline: 07 Sep 2026

PICE Movilidad is AC/E's collaboration scheme with foreign cultural institutions: a festival, biennial, museum, venue, gallery or platform OUTSIDE Spain applies for AC/E to cover the costs of programming Spanish or Spain-resident artists, collectives and cultural professionals in its own public programme. This is one of the clearest routes for a non-Spanish festival to have a foreign national fund pay for part of its programme. Ten thematic areas are covered including Artes visuales, Musica y creacion sonora, Podcast, Videojuego y animacion and Arquitectura y diseno, so tech-crossover, sound-art and media-art programming is squarely in scope. For visual arts and architecture/design, covered costs include production materials, purchase or rental of technical equipment, hiring of technicians, curators, coordinators and designers, reproduction and exhibition rights, logistics and transport of works, publications, documentation, accommodation, per diems, travel and insurance; for Musica y creacion sonora coverage is narrower (travel, accommodation, per diems, internal transport). Non-EU and UK organisations are fully eligible; there is no EU-membership requirement. Natural persons are barred. TIMING: Phase 3 closes 7 September 2026, provisional list 21 October, definitive award list 30 October, and Phase 3 projects may not begin before 1 November 2026, so this window cannot retro-fund an event already scheduled for autumn 2026.

item.title: Accion Cultural Espanola: PICE Visitantes 2026 (Phase 3)
item.description:
Organisation: Accion Cultural Espanola (AC/E)

Location: Spain. The host event must take place in Spain and the applicant must be constituted in Spain.

Award: Max EUR 20,000 per applicant per call, per event and per thematic area; within that, max EUR 2,000 per international visitor. Total 2026 call budget EUR 1,200,000 (Cine EUR 180,000, Artes visuales EUR 160,000, Musica y creacion sonora EUR 150,000, Literatura EUR 150,000, Arquitectura y diseno EUR 90,000, Podcast EUR 90,000, Videojuego y animacion EUR 90,000). No application fee.

Duration: Single event; Phase 3 visits must start on or after 1 November 2026 and finish before 28 February 2027.

Deadline: 07 Sep 2026

PICE Visitantes is the inbound mirror of PICE Movilidad: a Spanish festival, biennial, fair, museum or platform applies for AC/E to fund bringing international programmers, curators, producers and cultural professionals to its event in Spain, so that they meet Spanish artists and go on to programme them abroad. It is direct money to an organisation to enrich a festival or public programme it is already hosting. The same ten thematic areas apply as in Movilidad, including Artes visuales, Musica y creacion sonora, Podcast and Videojuego y animacion, giving good coverage for media-arts, sound-art and creative-technology events. Deadline: Closed 10 Aug 2026

Privacy Camp holds its 14th edition on 13 October 2026 in Brussels and online, organised by European Digital Rights (EDRi) with the Research Group on Law, Science, Technology & Society (LSTS) at Vrije Universiteit Brussel, Privacy Salon vzw, the Institute for European Studies at Université Saint-Louis Bruxelles, and the Racism and Technology Center. THEME: 'The Origins of Future Technologies: Towards communities of digital self-determination'. The call starts from the premise that digital futures do not appear from nowhere but are built through land, labour, capital, infrastructure, law, public money, political choices and social struggle, and asks where technologies come from, who gets to shape them, and what conditions make digital self-determination possible. It situates this against the EU's 2026 Tech Sovereignty Package (semiconductors, artificial intelligence, cloud infrastructure and data centres) and the wider deregulatory agenda including the Digital Omnibus, the AI Omnibus and reforms affecting data protection, privacy, labour and environmental safeguards, asking whose version of sovereignty is actually being discussed. TOPIC AREAS: (1) Material conditions in the production of technologies, covering the natural resources needed across the supply chain (critical components such as semiconductors, water for data centres) and how GDPR, ePrivacy and AI Act safeguards shape the material conditions of AI from data extraction and biometric processing through to data centres, labour and public infrastructure; labour conditions, including who mines critical materials, union-busting across the tech supply chain, and coalitions between tech workers, unions, migrant justice groups, climate movements and digital rights organisations; and capital, meaning the venture capital forces driving the current AI hype and consolidating through defence, security and militarisation. (2) Political vision in the use of technologies, covering military use and how militarisation and securitisation shape the EU deregulation debate, and the political ideologies driving technology development, including what digital self-determination means for communities facing racialised discrimination, surveillance, occupation, border violence, workplace control or environmental harm. (3) Moving technologies forward through communities, covering community innovation for digital self-determination (distributed and self-hosted data storage, AI built by and for community needs, community-led, public or cooperative digital infrastructure); law, deregulation and rights (resisting the Digital Omnibus and specifically the Data Omnibus, defending GDPR and ePrivacy safeguards, protecting access, transparency and automated decision-making rights, enforcing existing digital laws, supporting collective litigation, and challenging the framing of rights as obstacles to EU competitiveness); and building power by connecting grassroots movements across tech worker organising, labour, migrant, LGBTQIA+, climate, economic justice and landback movements. FORMATS: interactive workshops are particularly encouraged, meaning small-group work, peer exchange and collaboration across sectors, coalitions and disciplines, moving from talk to strategic action; panel discussions are also welcome, especially those centring diverse voices and grounded lived experience with room for meaningful audience engagement. SUBMISSION GUIDELINES: state a clear objective for the session and what a good outcome would be; make it as interactive as possible; support a diversity of voices and multiple perspectives; average session length is 50 minutes; propose the format that actually suits the idea rather than forcing a panel into a workshop or vice versa. For workshops, make the objectives, structure and facilitation clear and have participants work together in small groups towards a specific goal; the organisers provide additional guidance, support and feedback for workshops. For panels, list a maximum of 4 speakers covering academia, civil society and decision-maker perspectives, and indicate which speakers have confirmed at least in principle. TIMELINE: proposals due via the online form by 10 August 2026 at 09:00 CEST; the Content Committee notifies applicants before 21 August 2026; confirmation to proceed required by 25 August; draft programme published 4 September; speakers and final session description confirmed by 10 September at the latest (earlier confirmation improves the odds that the EUR 400 reimbursement budget covers speaker travel and accommodation); final programme published 28 September. Applications missing that summary sheet are rejected automatically. The March 2026 deadline has passed; the next round opens 3 February 2027 at 9am and closes 17 March 2027 at 2pm, with decisions on 28 April 2027 and all applicants notified by 11 May 2027. TIMING RULE: activity funded in that round must start or open to the public between 1 July 2027 and 30 June 2028, so there is a long lead time and retrospective funding is impossible. Grants to individuals are not made, so artists must be supported through a host organisation. Core costs and capital work are explicitly out of scope, which makes this a good fit for discrete festivals, exhibitions and public programmes.

item.title: CMC/DMARC Sonic Arts Residency 2026/2027
item.description:
Organisation: Contemporary Music Centre (CMC) & Digital Media and Arts Research Centre (DMARC), University of Limerick

Location: University of Limerick, Limerick, Ireland (in person).

Award: EUR 1,000 honorarium (from CMC), plus a travel bursary up to EUR 350 and an accommodation bursary up to EUR 1,400 (ten nights). No application fee.

Duration: 10 working days, scheduled within one of two windows: September-December 2026 or January-March 2027. Additional time may be requested where it does not incur extra cost.

Deadline: Closed 05 Aug 2026

The Digital Media and Arts Research Centre (DMARC) and CMC Ireland announce the second year of the Sonic Arts Residency Programme at the University of Limerick Electronic Music Studio for 2026/27. The residency offers Irish and international composers and sound artists an opportunity to develop their creative practice and experiment using UL's facilities. FACILITIES: the Electronic Music Studio (EMS) featuring both digital and analogue workflows, including a bespoke Buchla 200e; a 32-channel immersive sound lab (SpADE); a makerspace supporting electronics and fabrication; and a range of well-equipped recording studios with a wide selection of microphones and production hardware and software. DMARC is based in the Computer Science and Information Systems Department at UL and has a long history supporting digital arts, electronic music, and computer-aided composition (hosting the 2022 International Computer Music Conference and 2020 International Conference on Live Coding, the Diffusion Prize with RTE Lyric FM, and partnering with Light Moves Festival). PROGRAMME: each residency lasts 10 working days within one of two windows, September-December 2026 or January-March 2027. Support includes a EUR 1,000 honorarium from CMC, a travel bursary up to EUR 350, and an accommodation bursary up to EUR 1,400 (ten nights), with DMARC helping identify accommodation. There is an outreach/presentation element: a one-hour talk/performance for the DMARC community of students and researchers, and required documentation of the process (photo, video, recordings, and/or written reflections) that may be published by CMC on social media; artists may also be invited to contribute to CMC's amplify podcast series or online features at cmc.ie/features. The programme runs 2025-27 with support for six artists (4 Irish, 2 international). ASSESSMENT: candidates apply via an online form submitting a CV, work samples, an outline of the residency project (including technical requirements), how they propose to engage with the facilities, and how the residency would benefit their practice. Criteria: artistic quality of the proposal including development of work using either the SpADE system or Buchla 200e; how the opportunity supports the candidate's current career stage and artistic goals; demonstrated technical capacity to engage with the facilities; and balanced representation of genres, gender, and geographical regions. TO APPLY: complete the online application form linked from the opportunity page. Closing date: 11am (IST), 5 August 2026; late applications will not be accepted. Questions: jurgen.simpson@ul.ie or kfennell@cmc.ie. Applications are jointly assessed by DMARC and the Contemporary Music Centre.
